what_its_for: Dupilumab is used to treat certain inflammatory conditions by calming an overactive immune response. It is approved for moderate-to-severe eczema (atopic dermatitis), asthma (when not controlled by other inhalers), chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (persistent nasal congestion and growths in your nose), eosinophilic esophagitis (inflammation of the swallowing tube), prurigo nodularis (itchy skin bumps), and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in certain patients. It works by blocking specific proteins (IL-4 and IL-13) that cause inflammation in your body.
how_to_take: Dupilumab is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection). It comes in a pre-filled syringe or an auto-injector pen. You or a caregiver can give the injection at home after proper training from your doctor or nurse. Common injection sites include the front of your thighs, your belly (at least 2 inches away from the belly button), or the back of the upper arm (only if someone else gives the injection). Rotate injection sites each time and never inject into skin that is tender, bruised, red, hard, scarred, or damaged. Allow the medicine to sit at room temperature for 30 to 45 minutes before injecting — never heat it up. Clean the injection site with an alcohol wipe and let it dry before injecting.
dosing: Your dose depends on your age, weight, and the condition being treated. For most adults with eczema, the typical starting dose is 600 mg (two 300 mg injections given at the same time), followed by 300 mg every other week. For asthma and nasal polyps, the usual adult dose is 200 mg or 300 mg every other week, or 300 mg every 4 weeks, depending on your situation. For children, the dose is based on body weight and your doctor will determine the right schedule. Always follow your doctor's exact dosing instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember, as long as it is within 7 days of your missed dose. Then go back to your regular schedule. If more than 7 days have passed since your missed dose, skip the missed dose and inject your next dose on the regularly scheduled day. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store dupilumab in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it, and do not use it if it has been frozen. Once removed from the refrigerator, it can be kept at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 14 days. After 14 days at room temperature, throw it away even if there is medicine remaining. Do not put it back in the refrigerator after it has been stored at room temperature. Keep out of reach of children. Do not shake the medicine.
what_to_avoid: Do not receive live vaccines (such as MMR, chickenpox, or nasal flu vaccine) while using dupilumab without first talking to your doctor. Avoid injecting into skin that is irritated, broken, or has a rash. Do not stop using dupilumab suddenly without talking to your doctor, as your symptoms may return. If you use eye drops for a condition related to eczema, continue using them as directed unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: signs of a serious allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face, lips, mouth or throat, difficulty breathing, or feeling faint; eye problems including new or worsening redness, itching, pain, or changes in vision (these can be signs of eye inflammation called conjunctivitis or keratitis); joint pain or swelling (arthritis-like symptoms); signs of infection such as fever, chills, or a wound that will not heal; or any new or worsening symptoms after starting the medication. Also contact your doctor if you experience injection site reactions that are severe or do not go away.
when_it_works: Most people begin to notice some improvement within 2 to 4 weeks of starting dupilumab, but the full benefit may take 3 to 6 months or longer. For eczema, you may notice less itching and skin clearing within the first few weeks. For asthma and nasal polyps, breathing and congestion may start improving within the first month. Be patient and continue using the medication as prescribed even if you do not see immediate results. Do not stop using it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. There is a pregnancy registry available — ask your doctor about it. Dupilumab should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed and after discussing the risks and benefits with your doctor. Children: Dupilumab is approved for certain children as young as 6 months old for eczema, and for children 6 years and older for other approved conditions. Dosing for children is based on weight. Elderly (65 years and older): No dose adjustment is needed, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: No dose adjustment is currently required, but always tell your doctor about any kidney or liver issues you have.
